_schema: testId, environment, procedure, expectedResult, observedResult, status, evidenceRef, operatorNotes

automated.observedResult: 1 display detected (Xvfb's single virtual screen) - see ../../hardware-status.json (Phase 3.3) and ../software/xvfb-relaunch-3.4-run1-fresh.log and ../software/xvfb-relaunch-3.4-run2-idempotent.log
automated.operatorNotes: This proves the DisplayDiagnostic code path (including the new Phase 3.4 positionX/positionY fields) executes correctly - never physical-display evidence. Xvfb reports exactly one screen; this container cannot simulate a second monitor.

realHardwareRequired.procedure: Connect a second monitor/projector to the HP EliteBook 830 G6 (HDMI/USB-C/DisplayPort as available)

realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: displays.len() == 2, with real width/height/position/scaleFactor for the projector

realHardwareRequired.procedure: Open the presentation display window, move it to the second display
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: Window opens on the projector, not the operator's laptop screen

realHardwareRequired.procedure: Activate a short verse (e.g. John 3:16) on the presentation display
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: Scripture readable at normal operator/congregation distance, correct reference, no clipping/overflow, adequate contrast

realHardwareRequired.procedure: Update to a second, longer verse/passage
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: Correct line wrapping, no stale text, no accidental blank screen
Display clears/closes as expected, no crash

realHardwareRequired.procedure: Close and physically disconnect the display, then reconnect
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: CIP recovers gracefully (WindowEvent::Destroyed reconciliation path - see presentation_display.rs) - no stale Active presentation, no crash
realHardwareRequired.operatorNotes: The reconciliation logic itself is proven at the code level (Environment A) - see automated-regression.json presentation tests. Only the real-monitor-disconnect trigger is BLOCKED.

realHardwareRequired.procedure: Test at whatever resolution the target projector actually supports (720p / 1080p / other)
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: Readability confirmed at the real resolution used - not assumed from a different resolution
